statement.p: Find the vertices, foci, axes, center (if an ellipse or a hyperbola) and asymptotes (if a hyperbola) of the conic section x^2+4 y^2 = 16

The conic section is
An ellipse
A Parabola
A hyperbola

The focal axis and the conjugate axis are
y=0 and x=0 respectively.
x=0 and y=0 respectively.
y=4 and x=16 respectively.
x=16 and y=4 respectively.

The conic section's center is at
(-4,-4)
(0,0)
(4,4)
(4,16)
(1,1)

static.solution:
16 to convert it to the equation in standard form: \frac{{x}^{2}}{16}+\frac{4 {y}^{2}}{16}=1 \Rightarrow \frac{{x}^{2}}{16}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}=1 \Rightarrow {\left(\frac{x}{4}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{y}{\sqrt{4}}\right)}^{2}=1 For this ellipse, a=4 and b=\sqrt{4} hence c=\sqrt{{4}^{2}-\left(\sqrt{4}\right)^2}=\sqrt{12}.
Since a>b we have:
\bullet The vertices are at \left(\pm 4, 0\right),\left(0, \pm \sqrt{4}\right).
\bullet The foci are {F}_{1}=\left(-\sqrt{12}, 0\right) and {F}_{2}=\left(\sqrt{12}, 0\right).
\bullet The focal axis is the x-axis and the conjugate axis is the y-axis.
\bullet The ellipse is centered at the origin.
